slides.texte_overlay:
7 social hacks that feel
like cheating when you travel
Learn hello, thank you and sorry in the local language before you land. Say them with a smile, even badly. People switch from tourist mode to friendly mode the second you try.
Ask locals "Where do you eat?" instead of "What's good around here?" The first gets you the place their family goes. The second gets you the restaurant with the menu in six languages.
Sit at the bar, not at a table, when you eat alone. The bartender talks to you, the people next to you talk to you, and you leave with three recommendations and maybe a new friend.
Compliment something specific to the place. "Your city has the best bread I've ever had." People are proud of where they're from, and that one line opens more doors than any guidebook.
Offer to take photos for other travelers. "Want me to get one of you both?" It's the easiest icebreaker on earth, and half the time they ask where you're from and invite you along.
Learn a little about the place before you go. The local hero, the famous dish, one historical story. Locals light up when a visitor actually knows something real about their home.
Know a little about everything. Five minutes a day of history, art or science and every trip gets better. You walk past old buildings and actually know why they matter. Locals notice.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now every trip is better. I walk past old buildings and actually know why they matter.
